question: Will Bolivia's Supreme Decree 5716 (the diesel subsidy cut) be abrogated or suspended by October 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is no abrogation: government repeatedly and explicitly refuses (Blanco Sept 26, Justiniano), IMF EFF approved Oct 2 with immediate $214M disbursement tied to subsidy removal, technical implementation ongoing (Asosur talks Oct 4). Opposition is broad but fragmented: drivers in dialogue, Santa Cruz transport suspended its Oct 5-6 strike, COB only convening; Evo's mobilization only starts Oct 13, leaving ~2-4 days before the Oct 15-17 window, under a state of exception banning blockades. Upward risk: Paz has a record of formal reversals (abrogated DS 5503 in Jan 2026 after ~4 weeks of COB blockades, replaced by DS 5516 keeping prices; annulled Law 1720 in May 2026), and abrogate-and-replace would count YES. But 5716 is a single-purpose price decree with no extraneous articles to trade, and the window is short. No human prediction market found.
calls.dossier:
- DS 5716 signed 18 Sep 2026: diesel Bs 9.80 -> Bs 17.95/L, indexed to import parity with +-5% adjustment band (urgente.bo; Rio Times).
- Govt stance: Hydrocarbons Min. Blanco 26 Sep: 'the decree will not be abrogated', cites ~$200M subsidy cost (La Razon). Govt ratified no abrogation while inviting drivers to dialogue (El Deber, late Sep). Govt Min./Defence Min.: 'nobody is above the law' re Evo ultimatum (eju.tv, Infobae 27 Sep).
- IMF Executive Board approved ~$1.9B 3-yr EFF on Fri 2 Oct 2026 with immediate ~$214M disbursement (La Razon, Los Tiempos 2 Oct).
- Implementation continuing: Hydrocarbons Ministry and Asosur set up permanent technical meetings on new pricing methodology, 4 Oct (La Razon).
- Opposition: Confederacion de Choferes 24h national strike 28 Sep (Santa Cruz paralyzed, La Paz/El Alto operated); govt-drivers dialogue opened 29 Sep in La Paz, drivers' main demand = abrogation; govt offering CNG conversion, fleet-renewal credit. Santa Cruz transport threatened 48h strike 5-6 Oct but on Sat 3 Oct suspended it pending meeting with national authorities (Vision360/El Deber/Exito Noticias). Urban teachers marched 30 Sep-1 Oct. Fencomin (mining coops) declared national mobilization 30 Sep, also demanding two ministers resign. COB rejected 'dieselazo' and convened ampliado (Los Tiempos 19 Sep); fabriles urged COB to define actions. Church (Archbishop Galvan) offered mediation.
- Evo Morales (fugitive with arrest warrant, in Lauca N) gave deadline 3 Oct to abrogate DS 5716 and DS 5727; threatens 'great national mobilization' from Tue 13 Oct.
- State of exception banning road blockades in force to 17 Dec 2026.
- Precedents for this govt: Paz abrogated DS 5503 (fuel subsidy omnibus, Dec 2025) on ~12 Jan 2026 after ~4 weeks of COB strikes/blockades, via agreement with COB; replaced by DS 5516 (13 Jan) which KEPT the fuel price increases and dropped other contested articles (Unitel, Vision360, Correo del Sur). Paz annulled Law 1720 (land) on 13 May 2026 amid protests (Wikipedia 2026 Bolivian protests). Under this question, an abrogate-and-replace would count as YES.
- Difference vs 5503: 5716 is a narrow price decree; 5503 was an omnibus with many non-fuel articles that were traded away.
- Historical: 2010 gasolinazo (Morales) reversed within ~5 days of mass protests.
- Base rates: over Paz govt's major contested economic norms in 2026 (DS 5503, Law 1720), both were eventually formally reversed, but 5503 took ~4 weeks of intense blockades; over LatAm fuel-subsidy removals with mass protest, formal reversal is a minority outcome (Ecuador 2019 reversed in ~11 days; Ecuador 2023/24 and Nigeria 2023 held; Bolivia 2010 reversed in days).
- Resolution instrument: resolves off formal abrogation/derogation/suspension of DS 5716 (new DS in Gaceta Oficial or official announcement); price cuts, sector subsidies, methodology changes leaving 5716 in force do NOT count.
- Event window: 15 Oct 2026 -> 17 Oct 2026 (measure in force at any point in window; an earlier abrogation still in force would plausibly count); as of 5 Oct 2026, window not yet started; ~12 days remain to end.
- Searched but not found: any govt signal of a replacement norm; COB general-strike date; any prediction market (Polymarket/Manifold none per harness; none found otherwise).
calls.reference_class: Latin American fuel-subsidy removals facing mass protest, reversed formally within ~4 weeks of enactment; plus Paz government's own record of formal reversals under protest

calls.reasoning: Status quo is the decree staying in force; the government has repeatedly and explicitly refused repeal (Blanco, Justiniano, Sept 29 talks ended without agreement), and the IMF board approved the program on Oct 2 with an immediate ~$214m disbursement, which strengthens lock-in. A state of exception banning blockades runs to Dec 17. Pointing the other way, the same Paz government repealed fuel decree DS 5503 in Jan 2026 after about 2 weeks of COB protests, while keeping the prices, and a repeal-and-replace move like that would resolve YES. The main escalation (Morales's mobilization) starts Oct 13, leaving only about 2-4 days before the Oct 15-17 window, so a capitulation that fast is unlikely. No human prediction market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- DS 5716 (Sept 18, 2026) ended the diesel subsidy, moving the price from Bs 9.80 to Bs 17.95 and tying it to import parity with a +/-5% band. It was signed hours after the Senate approved the IMF credit (France24, RioTimes, Sept 19).
- Hydrocarbons Minister Blanco ruled out abrogation on Sept 26, saying the subsidy cost about $200m (La Razon, ABI). Defense Minister Justiniano told Evo Morales 'nobody is above the law' (Infobae, Sept 27).
- Sept 29 national drivers' confederation talks in La Paz: the government kept the decree and offered sector working groups, natural-gas vehicle conversion and credit. No agreement (El Deber, Los Tiempos, Sept 29-30).
- Santa Cruz transport gave a 48-hour ultimatum and called a 48-hour strike for Oct 5-6 (El Deber, Sept 29). The outcome was not found. Earlier, on Sept 20, the government defused a Santa Cruz strike with a sector deal that left the decree in place (ABI).
- Fencomin (mining cooperatives) declared national mobilization on Sept 30 and demanded the resignation of two ministers. Urban teachers marched Sept 30 to Oct 1. The COB rejected the decree and called an emergency national assembly (Unitel, Los Tiempos, Sept 19). No COB general strike date was found.
- Morales gave a deadline of Oct 3 and set mobilization (marches, strikes, blockades) from Oct 13, coinciding with Chilean President Kast's visit (La Razon, Sept 26 and 28).
- The IMF board approved the $1.9bn EFF on Oct 2 with an immediate ~$214m disbursement. Bolivia committed to eliminating fuel subsidies by early 2027 (Los Tiempos, El Dia, Oct 2).
- A state of exception banning blockades runs to Dec 17. Police cleared a Beni farmers' blockade, injuring at least 5 (RioTimes).
- Precedent within this government: DS 5503 (Dec 2025 fuel subsidy removal) was fully repealed around Jan 12-13, 2026, after about 2 weeks of COB protests. A commission was formed and prices were reportedly kept (UPI, Jan 13, 2026; RioTimes).
- Precedent: the 2010 gasolinazo under Morales was reversed within about 5 days. Ecuador's 2019 decree 883 was reversed in about 11 days.
- Resolution: resolves off a new supreme decree in the Gaceta Oficial or an official government announcement of abrogation or suspension. It does not count price cuts, partial sector subsidies or compensation measures that leave 5716 in force. A repeal-and-replace move would count.
- Event window: abrogation or suspension in force at any point from Oct 15 to Oct 17, 2026 (Bolivia time), effectively a deadline of end of Oct 17. As of Oct 5, about 12 days remain. Major escalation is scheduled from Oct 13, roughly 2-4 days before the deadline.
- Searched for but not found: any news from Oct 3-5 (outcome of the Santa Cruz strike, government reply to Morales's deadline), a COB strike date, and any prediction market (none on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi).
calls.reference_class: Latin American/Bolivian fuel-subsidy removals facing mass protest (2010 gasolinazo reversed in 5 days; Ecuador 2019 reversed in about 11 days; Jan 2026 DS 5503 repealed after about 2-3 weeks; many others held, e.g. Ecuador 2023-24 and Argentina), restricted to reversals occurring within about 4 days

Base rate from Bolivian fuel-subsidy-cut decrees under mass protest (2010 gasolinazo, Paz's own DS 5503 abrogated Jan 2026 after ~4 weeks of COB blockades) is high, ~25%, but those reversals required broad COB-led blockades; here COB has only held assemblies, the Sept 28 strike was patchy outside Santa Cruz, and Evo's mobilization begins only Oct 13, leaving 2-4 days before the window closes. calls.reasoning: The status quo is that DS 5716 stays in force. Ministers Blanco and Justiniano have refused repeal more than once. The IMF EFF was approved on 2 Oct with a disbursement tied to removing fuel subsidies, and technical work on the pricing method continues. A state of exception bans blockades until 17 Dec. The opposition is broad but fragmented: drivers are in talks, Santa Cruz transport reportedly suspended its 5-6 Oct strike, and the COB has not set a general strike date. Morales's mobilization starts 13 Oct, only 2-4 days before the window closes. The upside risk is Paz's record of formal reversals (DS 5503 repealed and replaced in Jan 2026, Law 1720 annulled), and a repeal-and-replace would count as YES. But DS 5503 took weeks of COB-led blockades, and DS 5716 is a narrow price decree with no side articles to trade away. No human prediction market was found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the core facts: the government refuses repeal, the IMF approved the program on 2 Oct, the state of exception runs to 17 Dec, Morales mobilizes from 13 Oct, and DS 5503 was repealed in Jan 2026. Factual disputes: (1) Whether the Santa Cruz 5-6 Oct strike happened. Run 1 cites a 3 Oct suspension pending talks; Runs 2 and 3 did not find the outcome. I accept Run 1's more specific dated report, with moderate confidence. It points slightly toward de-escalation. (2) How long the DS 5503 reversal took: about 2 weeks (Run 2) versus about 4 weeks (Runs 1 and 3). DS 5503 dates from mid-December 2025 and was repealed around 12-13 Jan 2026, so the period from issue to repeal was about 4 weeks, though the intense blockade phase may have been shorter. Either way, it needed sustained COB blockades, and none have yet been called against DS 5716. The rest is judgment about how fast Paz could fold once escalation starts on 13 Oct. The window is short and the IMF lock-in is fresh, so I place the estimate in the middle of the runs' range, at 7%. I retrieved nothing myself on this run.
